results.name: Barbell Good Morning
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell across your upper back. Grip the bar with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Slightly bend your knees and hinge at your hips to lower your torso forward. Keep your back straight and your head in line with your spine.
Continue to lower your torso until it is nearly parallel to the floor, feeling a stretch in your hamstrings and glutes.
Engage your glutes and hamstrings to raise your torso back to the starting position, keeping your back straight and core engaged. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Maintain a neutral spine throughout the movement to prevent lower back strain.
Engage your core to support your lower back and maintain stability.
Hinge at your hips rather than bending your back to ensure proper form.
results.description: Barbell Good Morning is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Glutes.

results.name: Barbell Long Landmine Row
instructions: Set up a barbell in a landmine attachment or securely place one end of the barbell in a corner. Stand to the side of the barbell with your feet shoulder-width apart, barbell extending behind. Bend at the hips and knees, keeping your back straight, and grip the barbell with your hand.
Start with your arm fully extended, allowing the barbell to hang straight down.
Pull the barbell towards your side by bending your elbow and squeezing your back at the peak of the movement.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position, fully extending your arm. Repeat the movement for the desired repetitions.
tips: Maintain a neutral spine throughout the exercise to avoid straining your lower back.
Engage your core to help stabilize your body and prevent unnecessary movement.
Use a controlled motion to lift and lower the barbell, preventing any jerking movements.
results.description: Barbell Long Landmine Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Biceps, Lower Back.

results.name: Barbell Lying Row
instructions: Lie face down on a flat bench, holding a barbell with an overhand grip (palms facing down), hands placed shoulder-width apart. Your chest should be supported by the bench, and your feet should be firmly on the floor.
Let the barbell hang directly below you with your arms fully extended. Pull the barbell towards your lower chest by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position by extending your arms fully. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back flat and avoid rounding your shoulders or lower back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement to maximize upper back engagement.
Use a weight that allows for proper form and control throughout the exercise to prevent injury.
results.description: Barbell Lying Row is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Middle Back.

results.name: Barbell Meadows Row
instructions: Set up a barbell in a landmine attachment or securely place one end of the barbell in a corner. Stand perpendicular to the barbell with your feet shoulder-width apart. Bend at the hips and knees, keeping your back straight, and grip the barbell with your hand.
Start with your working arm fully extended, allowing the barbell to hang straight down.
Pull the barbell towards your lower ribs by bending your elbow and squeezing your back at the peak of the movement.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position, fully extending your arm. Repeat the movement for the desired repetitions.
tips: Squeeze your shoulder blade at the top of the movement to enhance muscle activation.
Adjust the weight on the barbell to challenge your muscles without compromising your form.
Ensure the landmine setup is secure to prevent slipping or tipping.
results.description: Barbell Meadows Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Biceps, Lower Back.

results.name: Barbell One Arm Single Deadlift
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a barbell with one hand using an overhand grip (palms facing your body). The barbell should be placed to the side of your body.
Begin the movement by hinging at your hips and slightly bending your knees, lowering the barbell towards the floor while keeping it close to your body.
Lower the barbell until before it touches the floor. Push through your heel to return to the starting position, extending your hips and knees fully while keeping your back straight.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.
tips: Keep the barbell close to your body to ensure an efficient and powerful lift.
Ensure your shoulders remain square to avoid twisting your torso and maintain proper alignment.
Use a weight that allows for proper form and control throughout the exercise to prevent strain or injury.
results.description: Barbell One Arm Single Deadlift is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Upper Back.

results.name: Barbell Pendlay Row
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a barbell with an overhand grip (palms facing down), hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Bend at the hips and knees to lower your torso until it is parallel to the floor.
Begin the row by pulling the barbell towards your abdomen, driving your elbows up and back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement, ensuring the barbell lightly touches your abdomen.
Lower the barbell back to the floor with control, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back flat and avoid rounding your shoulders to ensure proper form.
Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement to maximize back muscle activation.
Use a weight that allows for proper form and control throughout the exercise to prevent strain or injury.
results.description: Barbell Pendlay Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms.

results.name: Barbell Push Bent Over Row
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with palms facing the barbell, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Bend at the hips and knees to lower your torso until it is nearly parallel to the floor.

Pull the barbell towards your abdomen by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together. At the peak of the movement, perform a small push of the barbell downwards and pull it up again.
Lower the barbell back to the starting position with control, extending your arms fully while keeping your back straight.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back flat and avoid rounding your shoulders to ensure proper form.
Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement to maximize back muscle activation.
Use a weight that allows for proper form and control throughout the exercise to prevent strain or injury.
results.description: Barbell Push Bent Over Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms.

results.name: Barbell Reverse Deadlift
instructions: Stand with your feet at shoulder-width apart facing away from the barbell.
Squat down and grip the barbell behind your legs with an overhand grip.
Begin the lift by pushing through your heels, extending your hips and knees to lift the barbell off the floor until you stand up straight.
Lower the barbell back to the starting position with control and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep the barbell close to your legs throughout the movement.
Push your hips back as you lower the barbell. Avoid rounding your lower back.
Keep your chest up and your core tight throughout the exercise.
Inhale as you lower the barbell and exhale as you stand up.
results.description: Barbell Reverse Deadlift is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Upper Back, Forearms.

results.name: Barbell Reverse Grip Bent Over Row
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with a reverse grip (palms facing forward), hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Bend at the hips and knees to lower your torso until it is nearly parallel to the floor, keeping your back straight and core engaged.
Pull the barbell towards your abdomen by bending your elbows.
Lower the barbell back to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement to maximize back muscle activation.
Use a weight that allows for proper form and control throughout the exercise to prevent strain or injury.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you pull the barbell up and inhaling as you lower it back down.
results.description: Barbell Reverse Grip Bent Over Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Biceps, Forearms.

results.name: Barbell Romanian Deadlift
instructions: Begin in a squat position with your feet hip-width apart, holding a barbell with an overhand grip (palms facing down), hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Stand up by driving through your heels and extending your hips and knees until you are standing straight with the barbell hanging in front of your thighs.

From this standing position, hinge at your hips and push them back, lowering the barbell down the front of your legs while keeping your back straight and knees slightly bent. Lower the barbell until it passes your knees.
Drive your hips forward to return to the standing position, lifting the barbell back up while keeping it close to your legs. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep the barbell close to your body to ensure an efficient and safe lift.
Focus on hinging at the hips rather than bending at the waist to properly target the hamstrings and glutes.
Control the descent of the barbell to maximize muscle engagement and prevent strain.
results.description: Barbell Romanian Deadlift is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Adductors.
